clue.text: Don't allow backing for Trump's extremes to overshadow right's regular following

indicators.note: to overshadow something is to loom over it on both sides, so the outer pair wraps the rest
backing is moving in reverse, so the kept pair is read from right to left
the extremes of a word are its two end letters, the first and the last

parts.note: the first and last letters of the name

indicators.note: one piece comes following the other, so they are simply set side by side in that order

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right
regular as in steady and uniform

explanation.surface: Someone urges stopping a supporter of Trump from overshadowing a loyal right-wing following.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing for Trump' reads like political support, but it means turning round the end letters of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it happening, which is refusing to let it take place.

clue.text: Time to support group deal

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so it comes second

parts.note: a pack is a group, as of wolves
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: It's time to back a group deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A package is a set of terms offered together, as in a package deal or pay package.

clue.text: Surround with trained men to guard company on way through mountains

indicators.note: one piece is put on after the other, so they follow in sequence
a guard stands around what it protects, so one piece encloses the other
something trained has been reshaped, so the next word's letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
standard abbreviation
a mountain pass is a route through a range

explanation.surface: Trained soldiers escort a company through a mountain route, surrounding it.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass something is to encircle or enclose it entirely on all sides.

clue.text: Times has note to delete

indicators.note: the first word has the next beside it, so the two join in order

parts.note: eras are periods of time
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper has a memo telling staff to delete something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it simply means periods of history.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to remove or wipe out, exactly what deleting text or data does.

clue.text: Valued guaranteed break in walk

indicators.note: to break in is to get inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to tread is to walk
sure means certain or guaranteed

explanation.surface: A cherished walk is certain to be interrupted by a rest stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like a pause in the walk, but it tells you to put one word inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasured is held dear and highly prized, which is what valued means.

clue.text: Most unhappy when daughters break new seats

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it, so one piece is placed within the other
something new has been remade, so the letters of the following word are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
D is the abbreviation for daughter, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A parent is at their gloomiest when the girls break the new chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Plurals of abbreviations are often doubled letters, as DD for daughters here.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddest is the superlative of sad, the state of being the most sorrowful or miserable.

clue.text: Sort of cabbage and soya stew goes round 5

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so the jumble wraps the other piece
a stew is a mixed-up dish, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A vegetarian stew of cabbage and soya, cooked with a numbered recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 is the number, not a cross-reference to 5-across or 5-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoy is a variety of cabbage with crinkled, dark green leaves.

clue.text: Powder coating's used to protect furniture

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun

parts.note: dust is fine powder
a coating covers a surface

explanation.surface: A powder coating is applied to furniture as protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the thing does rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust cover is a sheet draped over chairs and tables to keep dirt off them.

clue.text: Queen's taking King's gold — a mistake!

indicators.note: taking something means adding it on, so the pieces follow one another

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's cipher
R for Rex, Latin for king
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A queen helping herself to the king's gold is a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is something done wrongly, which is precisely what a mistake is.

clue.text: Criminal stole very quietly in and falls over

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other, sitting inside it
something criminal is crooked, so the next word's letters are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A burglar tiptoes in and trips over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that topples loses its balance and tips or falls to the ground.

clue.text: Clown has a drink before bed

indicators.note: one piece has the next beside it, so the two are joined in order

parts.note: Coco the Clown was a famous British circus clown
taken as written

explanation.surface: A circus clown enjoys a nightcap before turning in.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was a well-known Russian-born clown of the British circus.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot chocolate made with cocoa powder is a classic soothing nightcap taken before sleep.

clue.text: Overhear report of first lady's decline

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the words that follow are taken by their sound

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
a decline is a fall or drop

explanation.surface: Someone catches gossip about a First Lady's fall from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, Eve's drop is the same as EAVES DROP; the clue's 'first lady' looks political but means Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to a conversation, which is overhearing it deliberately.

clue.text: Same silly nonsense without any purpose

indicators.note: nonsense is jumbled talk, so the letters before it are put into a jumble

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: The same foolish talk drifts on without point.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something aimlessly means acting with no goal or direction in mind.

clue.text: Vocal about going ahead to see reef creatures

definitions.note: a mass noun for the many polyps

indicators.note: one piece going ahead of another is simply placed in front of it

parts.note: C for circa, Latin for about
spoken aloud rather than written

explanation.surface: Someone loudly urges a trip to see the creatures of a reef.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is made of colonies of tiny marine polyps, the living animals that build reefs.

clue.text: Demand English vote on legislation

parts.note: standard abbreviation
the cross marked on a ballot paper
an act of parliament is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: Someone calls for an English vote on a new law.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to insist on and obtain something, such as payment, from someone.

clue.text: Article about Brook is riveting

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: an article is an object or thing
a rill is a small stream or brook

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a person named Brook is gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a grammar word like A or THE; here it is an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Riveting means so exciting it holds your attention, just as a thrilling story does.

clue.text: Does up old veteran's junk

indicators.note: junk is a disordered heap of stuff, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: O is a common abbreviation for old
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone restores an old soldier's collection of clutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing up a house means repairing and refreshing it, restoring it to good condition.

clue.text: Out barking at the moon?

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the following letters go crazy

parts.note: the words taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog left outside howls at the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is British slang for mad, as in 'barking mad'.
explanation.definitionFit: If someone is out, they are away from their house and so absent when you call.

clue.text: Usage of a Dior tint's transforming!

indicators.note: transforming means changing form, so the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: the words taken as written

explanation.surface: Applying a Dior make-up tint is a dramatic makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage can mean established custom, a long-standing practice handed down over time.

clue.text: Cast doubt on record and run revision

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
an edit is a revision of a text

explanation.surface: A record and a run are revised, throwing doubt on a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a claim or person is to make them seem untrustworthy or doubtful.

clue.text: Expert help's required to go after flatfish

indicators.note: one piece going after another comes second in the sequence

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish
to give a hand is to help

explanation.surface: Specialist help is needed to catch a flounder-like fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A dab hand is British for someone skilled at something.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is a person who is very skilled at a particular task.

clue.text: Get to share a cheese sample

indicators.note: a sample is a small part taken from a larger whole, so the letters lie inside the phrase

parts.note: letters within the run of words

explanation.surface: Someone is invited to share a taste of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to arrive at it, getting there at last.

clue.text: Hospital leader's eyeing poor cleanliness

indicators.note: a leader is at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the next word's letters are out of order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital chief inspects poor standards of cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Hygiene is the practice of keeping clean to prevent disease, a matter of cleanliness.

clue.text: Bruised head's sore with long fight

indicators.note: the head of a word is its very front, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter
raw skin is sore and tender
L is the abbreviation for long

explanation.surface: A battered fighter is left with a sore, bruised head after a lengthy scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a rough, noisy fight, usually a scuffle involving several people.

clue.text: Part of Cambrian era's turned up in field

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top, the other way round
the letters are a part of the words that follow, lying inside them

parts.note: letters at the end of the phrase

explanation.surface: A fossil from the Cambrian period was dug up in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a field of activity or contest, as in the political arena.

clue.text: Wearisome fellow at first of Ireland's games nursing a half of Guinness

indicators.note: nursing something means holding it close, so the pair of initials holds the next piece between them

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written

indicators.note: the first of each of the two words that follow means only their opening letters

parts.note: the initials of the two words

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, so its back four letters are dropped

parts.note: the stout, taken as written before halving

explanation.surface: A man at Irish sporting games clutches a half-pint of the black stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A half of Guinness' sounds like a half-pint, but it means half the letters of the word; the two initials then hold that half between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fatiguing is tiring, wearing a person out, which is what wearisome describes.

clue.text: Iron a shirt, both sides, for banquet

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
taken as written

indicators.note: both sides of a word are its two edges, the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone presses a shirt on both sides ready for a formal dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' reads as a verb, but it is the metal, chemical symbol Fe.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a large, elaborate meal, the same thing as a banquet.

clue.text: Understand German artist's power

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a Royal Academician
the possessive ending taken as a letter
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone appreciates a German painter's strength.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to comprehend it, getting hold of it mentally.

clue.text: New Yorker, say, has love for black coffee …

indicators.note: the first piece has the second attached, so they are joined in sequence

parts.note: a New Yorker is an example of an American, as 'say' signals
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A New Yorker has a passion for strong black coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: An americano is espresso diluted with hot water, served without milk as a long black.

clue.text: … taking a fancy to similar!

parts.note: taken as written
to fancy something is to like it

explanation.surface: Following on from the coffee, someone takes a liking to it in kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots tie the surface to the previous clue; the definition is just the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are alike resemble each other closely, being much the same.

clue.text: Man on board is a breath of fresh air

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a playing piece in the board game ... (checkers)
second meaning: a current of air coming into a room

explanation.surface: A man aboard ship finds a pleasant, refreshing change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor, but a man is also a game piece; draughts is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is both a single checkers piece and a current of cool air through a gap.

clue.text: Cost is 10p, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the letters come from how the words sound

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten and p stands for pence

explanation.surface: A price tag reads ten pence, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 10p is ten pence; written with Roman X it reads 'ex pence'.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is money spent on something, the price or outlay paid for it.
